FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS.name: The character's name
FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS.title: A short epithet or title (e.g., "The Wanderer")
FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS.identity: What strangers know about the character on sight or by reputation — name, station, occupation, public reputation. The shallow first impression, and read only by others.
FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS.description: How acquaintances perceive the character — behaviour, mannerisms, frequent verbal patterns. Not physical appearance (that lives in physical descriptions), and never the inner monologue.
FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS.manifesto: The foundational tenets of this character — the basic truths that anchor everything else, delivered to the character alone. What this character is, at root.
FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS.personality: What the character knows about themselves — the inner drivers of speech and behaviour. Other characters don’t see it unless the character shows them.
FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS.scenarios: The setting and circumstances for conversations — the stage, never the actor. Generates 2-3 named scenarios with distinct settings.
FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS.exampleDialogues: Example conversations that model the character’s voice, as {{char}}: / {{user}}: exchanges — each line exactly as that speaker would say it.
FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS.firstMessage: The character’s opening message to start conversations, in their own voice.
FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS.systemPrompt: Stage direction for the model playing the character — voice, pacing, boundaries, interaction style — addressed to the character directly.
FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS.properties: Structured facts: pronouns and aliases (nicknames others use)
FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS.physicalDescription: Descriptive phrases only — this text also drives image generation, so keep to what a lens would record, never a sentence addressed to anyone. The person only — clothing lives in the wardrobe.
FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS.wardrobeItems: Clothing, accessories, hairstyles, and composite outfits (top, bottom, footwear, accessories, hair)
